57347-a-motor-flight-through-france.title: Through France
57347-a-motor-flight-through-france.creator: Edith Wharton
57347-a-motor-flight-through-france.description: A book by Edith Wharton. Freeing us from all the compulsions and contacts of the railway, the bondage to fixed hours and the beaten track, the approach to each town through the area of ugliness and desolation created by the railway itself, it has given us back the wonder, the adventure and the novelty which enlivened the way of our posting grand-parents.

arxiv-2103-05895.title: WFA-IRL: Inverse Reinforcement Learning of Autonomous Behaviors Encoded as Weighted Finite Automata
arxiv-2103-05895.creator: Tianyu Wang, Nikolay Atanasov
arxiv-2103-05895.description: Abstract This paper presents a method for learning logical task specifications and cost functions from demonstrations. Constructing specifications by hand is challenging for complex objectives and constraints in autonomous systems. Instead, we consider demonstrated task executions, whose logic structure and transition costs need to be inferred by an autonomous agent.

arxiv-2109-10491.title: Density estimates for the exponential functionals of fractional Brownian motion
arxiv-2109-10491.creator: Nguyen Tien Dung, Nguyen Thu Hang, Pham Thi Phuong Thuy
arxiv-2109-10491.description: Abstract In this note, we investigate the density of the exponential functional of the fractional Brownian motion. Based on the techniques of Malliavin’s calculus, we provide a log-normal upper bound for the density. Keywords: Fractional Brownian motion, Density estimates, Malliavin calculus. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 60G22, 60H07.

arxiv-2110-08687.title: Composite fermion mass enhancement and particle-hole symmetry of fractional quantum Hall states in the lowest Landau level under realistic conditions
arxiv-2110-08687.creator: Eduardo Palacios and Michael R. Peterson
arxiv-2110-08687.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Eduardo Palacios and Michael R. Peterson. Particle-hole symmetry breaking in the fractional quantum Hall effect has recently been studied both theoretically and experimentally with most works focusing on non-Abelian states in the second electronic Landau level. In this work, we theoretically investigate particle-hole symmetry breaking of incompressible fractional quantum Hall states in the lowest Landau level under the influence of the realistic effect of a finite magnetic field strength.

arxiv-2203-00666.title: Temporal Increments of the KPZ equation with general initial data
arxiv-2203-00666.creator: Sayan Das
arxiv-2203-00666.description: Abstract . We consider the Cole-Hopf solution of the (1+1)-dimensional KPZ equation ℋ f ​ ( t , x ) \mathcal{H}^{f}(t,x) started with initial data f f . In this article, we study the sample path properties of the KPZ temporal process ℋ t f := ℋ f ​ ( t , 0 ) \mathcal{H}_{t}^{f}:=\mathcal{H}^{f}(t,0) .

arxiv-2209-04178.title: Gapless states and current control in strongly distorted gated trilayer graphene
arxiv-2209-04178.creator: W. Jaskólski
arxiv-2209-04178.description: Abstract We investigate gated trilayer graphene partially devoid of outer layers and forming a system of two trilayers connected by a single layer of graphene. A difference in the stacking order of trilayers leads to the appearance of gapless states, one of which is mainly localized in the single graphene layer.

arxiv-2302-00507.title: Entropy determination for mixtures in the adiabatic grand-isobaric ensemble
arxiv-2302-00507.creator: Caroline Desgranges 4 and Jerome Delhommelle 1,2,3,4
arxiv-2302-00507.description: Abstract The entropy change that occurs upon mixing two fluids has remained an intriguing topic since the dawn of statistical mechanics. In this work, we generalize the grand-isobaric ensemble to mixtures, and develop a Monte Carlo algorithm for the rapid determination of entropy in these systems. A key advantage of adiabatic ensembles is the direct connection they provide with entropy.

arxiv-2302-14825.title: On the computational expressivity of (circular) proofs with fixed points
arxiv-2302-14825.creator: Gianluca Curzi ORCID:57216760760, Anupam Das ORCID:0000-0002-0142-3676
arxiv-2302-14825.description: Abstract . We study the computational expressivity of proof systems with fixed point operators, within the ‘proofs-as-programs’ paradigm. We start with a calculus μ ​ 𝖫𝖩 \mu\mathsf{LJ} (due to Clairambault) that extends intuitionistic propositional logic by least and greatest positive fixed points.

arxiv-2307-03763.title: Accelerating global parameter estimation of gravitational waves from Galactic binaries using a genetic algorithm and GPUs
arxiv-2307-03763.creator: Stefan H. Strub, Luigi Ferraioli, Cédric Schmelzbach, Simon C. Stähler, Domenico Giardini
arxiv-2307-03763.description: Abstract The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a planned space-based gravitational wave telescope with the goal of measuring gravitational waves in the milli-Hertz frequency band, which is dominated by millions of Galactic binaries. While some of these binaries produce signals that are loud enough to stand out and be extracted, most of them blur into a confusion foreground.

arxiv-2309-10800.title: Quantum Algorithm for Estimating Betti Numbers Using a Cohomology Approach
arxiv-2309-10800.creator: Nhat A. Nghiem, Xianfeng David Gu, Tzu-Chieh Wei
arxiv-2309-10800.description: Abstract Topological data analysis has emerged as a powerful tool for analyzing large-scale data. An abstract simplicial complex, in principle, can be built from data points, and by using tools from homology, topological features could be identified. Given a simplex, an important feature is called Betti numbers, which roughly count the number of ‘holes’ in different dimensions.

arxiv-2402-15995.title: Improved Hardness Results for Learning Intersections of Halfspaces Thanks: This project has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme (grant agreement No 815464).
arxiv-2402-15995.creator: Stefan Tiegel
arxiv-2402-15995.description: Abstract We show strong (and surprisingly simple) lower bounds for weakly learning intersections of halfspaces in the improper setting. Strikingly little is known about this problem. For instance, it is not even known if there is a polynomial-time algorithm for learning the intersection of only two halfspaces.

arxiv-2411-00557.title: Stellar surface information from the Ca II H&K lines - II. Defining better activity proxies
arxiv-2411-00557.creator: M. Cretignier, N.C. Hara, A.G.M. Pietrow, Y. Zhao, H. Yu, X. Dumusque, A. Sozzetti, C. Lovis, and S. Aigrain
arxiv-2411-00557.description: Abstract In our former paper I, we showed on the Sun that different active regions possess unique intensity profiles on the Ca II H & K lines. We now extend the analysis by showing how those properties can be used on real stellar observations, delivering more powerful activity proxies for radial velocity correction.

arxiv-2412-10506.title: Dense gas scaling relations at kiloparsec scales across nearby galaxies with the ALMA ALMOND and IRAM 30m EMPIRE surveys
arxiv-2412-10506.creator: Lukas Neumann ; María J. Jiménez-Donaire ; Frank Bigiel ; Adam K. Leroy ; Frank Bigiel ; Antonio Usero ; Jiayi Sun ; Eva Schinnerer ; Miguel Querejeta ; Sophia K. arxiv-2412-15383.title: DESI Mg II Absorbers: Extinction Characteristics & Quasar Redshift Accuracy
arxiv-2412-15383.creator: Lucas Napolitano, Adam D. Myers, Victoria A. Fawcett, Jessica Aguilar, Steven Ahlen, Davide Bianchi, David Brooks, Todd Claybaugh, Shaun Cole, Axel de la Macorra, Biprateep Dey, Andreu Font-Ribera, Jaime E. Forero-Romero, Enrique Gaztañaga, Satya Gontcho A Gontcho, Gaston Gutierrez, Klaus Honscheid,
arxiv-2412-15383.description: Abstract In this paper, we study how absorption-line systems affect the spectra and redshifts of quasars (QSOs), using catalogs of Mg II absorbers from the early data release (EDR) and first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI).

arxiv-2501-06658.title: Comparing Few-Shot Prompting of GPT-4 LLMs with BERT Classifiers for Open-Response Assessment in Tutor Equity Training
arxiv-2501-06658.creator: Sanjit Kakarla, Conrad Borchers, Danielle Thomas, Shambhavi Bhushan, Kenneth R. Koedinger
arxiv-2501-06658.description: Abstract Assessing learners in ill-defined domains, such as scenario-based human tutoring training, is an area of limited research. Equity training requires a nuanced understanding of context, but do contemporary large language models (LLMs) have a knowledge base that can navigate these nuances?

arxiv-2501-18525.title: Magnetically Assisted Vorticity Production in Decaying Acoustic Turbulence
arxiv-2501-18525.creator: Axel Brandenburg, Evan Scannapieco
arxiv-2501-18525.description: Abstract We study vorticity production in isothermal, subsonic, acoustic (nonvortical), and decaying turbulence due to the presence of magnetic fields. Using three-dimensional numerical simulations, we find that the resulting kinetic energy cascade follows the ordinary Kolmogorov phenomenology involving a constant spectral energy flux.

arxiv-2503-14606.title: Tidal dissipation in binary neutron star inspirals from hyperon bulk viscosity: Phase modeling and parameter estimation bias
arxiv-2503-14606.creator: Suprovo Ghosh, Samanwaya Mukherjee, Sukanta Bose, Debarati Chatterjee
arxiv-2503-14606.description: Abstract During the inspiral of a binary neutron star, viscous processes in the neutron star matter can damp out the tidal energy induced by its companion and convert it to thermal energy. This tidal dissipation/heating process introduces a net phase shift in the gravitational wave signal.

arxiv-2505-17696.title: Recovery speed
arxiv-2505-17696.description: Abstract This research proposes methods for formulating and guaranteeing the resilience of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, which can serve as a key technology in AI system quality assurance. We introduce a novel methodology applying incremental input-to-state stability ( δ \delta ISS) to mathematically define and evaluate the resilience of LSTM against input perturbations.

Relles, Chris Stockdale, John F. Kielkopf, Fabian Rodriguez Frustaglia, Allyson Bieryla, Joao Gregorio, Owen Mitchem, Katherine Linnenkohl, Adam Popowicz, Norio Narita, A. The eight-planet Kepler-90 system exhibits the greatest multiplicity of planets found to date. All eight planets are transiting and were discovered in photometry from the NASA Kepler primary mission.

arxiv-2508-17631.title: ControlEchoSynth: Boosting Ejection Fraction Estimation Models via Controlled Video Diffusion
arxiv-2508-17631.creator: Nima Kondori, Hanwen Liang, Hooman Vaseli, Bingyu Xie, Christina Luong, Purang Abolmaesumi, Teresa Tsang, Renjie Liao
arxiv-2508-17631.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nima Kondori, Hanwen Liang, Hooman Vaseli, Bingyu Xie, Christina Luong, Purang Abolmaesumi, Teresa Tsang, Renjie Liao. Synthetic data generation represents a significant advancement in boosting the performance of machine learning (ML) models, particularly in fields where data acquisition is challenging, such as echocardiography. The acquisition and labeling of echocardiograms (echo) for heart assessment, crucial in point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) settings, often encounter limitations due to the restricted number of echo views available, typically captured by operators with varying levels of experience.

arxiv-2509-16695.title: Picard groups of quotient ring spectra
arxiv-2509-16695.creator: Ishan Levy, Guchuan Li, Ningchuan Zhang
arxiv-2509-16695.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ishan Levy, Guchuan Li, Ningchuan Zhang. We develop tools to study Picard groups of quotients of ring spectra by a finitely generated ideal, which we use to show that Pic ⁡ ( E n / I ) = ℤ / 2 \mathrm{Pic}(\mathrm{E}_{n}/I)=\mathbb{Z}/2 , where E n \mathrm{E}_{n} is a Lubin–Tate theory and I I is an ideal generated by suitable powers of a regular sequence.

arxiv-2601-01995.title: Locally-averaged McCormick Relaxations for Discretization-regularized Inverse Problems
arxiv-2601-01995.creator: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Paul Manns
arxiv-2601-01995.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Barbara Kaltenbacher, Paul Manns. In this paper, by means of a standard model problem, we devise an approach to computing approximate dual bounds for use in global optimization of coefficient identification in partial differential equations (PDEs) by, e.g., (spatial) branch-and-bound methods. Linearization is achieved by a McCormick relaxation (that is, replacing the bilinear PDE term by a linear one and adding inequality constraints), combined with local averaging to reduce the number of inequalities.

arxiv-2602-17861.title: JAX-Privacy: A library for differentially private machine learning
arxiv-2602-17861.creator: Ryan McKenna, Galen Andrew, Borja Balle, Vadym Doroshenko, Arun Ganesh, Weiwei Kong, Alex Kurakin, Brendan McMahan, Mikhail Pravilov
arxiv-2602-17861.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The deployment of machine learning (ML) on sensitive data requires rigorous privacy guarantees to mitigate the risks of unintended memorization and membership inference. While Differential Privacy (DP) provides the necessary theoretical framework, there is a rich space of mechanisms to consider and implementation challenges to overcome to train private models effectively in practice.

The use of phages is an attractive option to battle antibiotic resistant bacteria in certain bacterial infections, but the role of phage ecology in bacterial infections is obscure. Tissue glucocorticoid levels in the liver and adipose tissue are regulated by regeneration of inactive glucocorticoid by 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11β-HSD1) and inactivation by 5α- and 5β-reductases. A low carbohydrate diet increases hepatic 11β-HSD1 and reduces gl

plos-pone-0011805.creator: Daniel Casasanto, Kyle Jasmin
plos-pone-0011805.description: PLOS ONE research article. According to the body-specificity hypothesis , people with different bodily characteristics should form correspondingly different mental representations, even in highly abstract conceptual domains. In a previous test of this proposal, right- and left-handers were found to associa

pmc-11442633.title: Sensitivity analysis and compensation for tooth surface deviation of spiral bevel gear machine tool
pmc-11442633.creator: Jianjun Yang, Linlin Si, Jubo Li, Wen Xin, Bo Zhao, Bingyang Wei
pmc-11442633.description: To analyze the quantitative mapping relationship between the geometric errors of the five-axis CNC machine tool and the tooth surface deviation of spiral bevel gears, and identify the key geometric errors that affect the machining deviation of the spiral bevel gear tooth surface, a sensitivity analysis method for tooth surface machining deviation of spiral bevel gear based on screw theory

pmc-11503303.title: A Novel Newborn Screening Program for Sickle Cell Disease in Nigeria
pmc-11503303.creator: Aisha A Galadanci, Umma A Ibrahim, Yvonne Carroll, Yusuf D Jobbi, Zubaida L Farouk, Aisha Mukaddas, Nafiu Hussaini, Bilya Sani Musa, Lauren J Klein, Michael R DeBaun, Amy Brower, Kee Chan
pmc-11503303.description: Newborn screening for sickle cell disease (SCD) is sparse in sub-Saharan Africa. The leadership of the Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH) in Kano, Nigeria, with the support of local religious authorities, established a groundbreaking SCD newborn screening program that has become the standard of care for pregnant women and their newborns.

pmc-11576853.title: CsWRKY29, a key transcription factor in tea plant for freezing tolerance, ABA sensitivity, and sugar metabolism
pmc-11576853.creator: Chengjin Xue, Xiaozhen Huang, Yichen Zhao
pmc-11576853.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tea plants (Camellia sinensis L.) are prone to spring frosts, leading to substantial economic damage. WRKY transcription factors are key in plant abiotic stress responses, yet the role of CsWRKY29 in freezing tolerance is unclear. In this study, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and transient green fluorescent protein assay revealed that CsWRKY29 localizes to the nucleus and its expression is induced by cold and abscisic acid (ABA).

pmc-11590813.title: Mapping inequalities in health service coverage in Africa: a scoping review
pmc-11590813.creator: Humphrey Cyprian Karamagi, Doris Osei Afriyie, Ali Ben Charif, Sokona Sy, Hillary Kipruto, Thandelike Moyo, Taiwo Oyelade, Benson Droti
pmc-11590813.description: ObjectiveIn this scoping review, we aim to consolidate the evidence on inequalities in service coverage in Africa using a comprehensive set of stratifiers. These stratifiers include place of residence, race/ethnicity/culture/language, occupation, gender/sex, religion, education, socioeconomic status and social capital. Our approach provides a more holistic understanding of the different dimensions of inequality in the context of universal health coverage (UHC).

pmc-12473775.title: Continuous Authentication in Resource-Constrained Devices via Biometric and Environmental Fusion
pmc-12473775.creator: Nida Zeeshan, Makhabbat Bakyt, Naghmeh Moradpoor, Luigi La Spada, Pietro Manzoni
pmc-12473775.description: Continuous authentication allows devices to keep checking that the active user is still the rightful owner instead of relying on a single login. However, current methods can be tricked by forging faces, revealing personal data, or draining the battery. Additionally, the environment where the user plays a vital role in determining the user’s online security.

pmc-12526864.title: Effects of Environmental Factors on the Performance of Ground-Based Low-Cost CO2 Sensors
pmc-12526864.creator: Xiaoyu Ren, Kai Wu, Dongxu Yang, Yi Liu, Yong Wang, Ting Wang, Zhaonan Cai, Lu Yao, Tonghui Zhao, Jing Wang, Zhe Jiang
pmc-12526864.description: This paper presents a multivariable linear regression calibration method for non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) CO2 sensors in a low-cost carbon monitoring network. We test this calibration method with data collected in a temperature- and pressure-controlled laboratory and evaluate the calibration method with long-term observational data collected at the Xinglong Atmospheric Background Observatory.

pmc-12583964.title: A review of risk assessment for driving in rainy weather
pmc-12583964.creator: Akram Ahmadizadeh Fini, Elham Ahmadizadeh Fini
pmc-12583964.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). :Background:Driving in rainy weather is considered one of the most challenging conditions due to potential hazards. Four key factors—human, vehicle, road, and environment—are always involved in accidents, with environmental factors and climatic phenomena playing a significant role. Therefore, this study aims to review and evaluate several studies conducted in this area as well as the main risk factors associated with driving in rainy conditions.

pmc-12609071.title: Optimising Green Pressurised Liquid Extraction and Sustainability Assessment of Carotenoid-Rich Extracts from Daucus carota L. Pomace
pmc-12609071.creator: Lidia Favaretto, Stefania Pagliari, Ciro Cannavacciuolo, Luca Campone, Massimo Labra
pmc-12609071.description: The increasing food waste generated along the food chain should be considered as a source of high-value compounds, with the aim of improving the circularity of productions. In this study, carrot pomace, the major by-product of carrot juice processing, was used as a source of carotenoids.

pmc-13183550.title: The antimicrobial potential of the secretome from Wharton’s jelly mesenchymal stem cells in the context of regenerative medicine: an in vitro study
pmc-13183550.creator: Filomena Napolitano, Emanuela Roscetto, Maria Fabozzi, Martina Aversa, Pietro Formisano, Maria Rosaria Catania, Nunzia Montuori
pmc-13183550.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe secretome derived from Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) have received significant attention as a promising tool in regenerative medicine. This “cell-free” strategy offers a promising alternative to stem cell therapies, potentially avoiding issues like immunogenicity and tumorigenicity. Recently, we demonstrated that MSC-conditioned media (MSC-CM) obtained from MSCs isolated from Wharton’s jelly (WJ) exerts notable bioactive effects associated with wound healing and tissue repair.

pmc-13313009.title: Clinical and Economic Burden Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for STEMI: A US Real-World Evidence Study
pmc-13313009.creator: Shanthi Krishnaswami, Brendan Clark, Manu Tyagi, Meenal Sinha, Bonnie M K Donato, Villum Wittrup-Jensen, Zhun Cao

pmc-13520867.title: Understanding competencies to manage multimorbidity in primary care: A focus group study with professionals and patients
pmc-13520867.creator: Leslie J Michielsen, Lena HA Raaijmakers, Miranda Laurant, Erik Bischoff, Geert M Rutten, Tjard R Schermer
pmc-13520867.description: BackgroundChronic conditions often occur as multimorbidity, where patients experience multiple chronic conditions simultaneously. Many developed countries have implemented disease management programmes (DMP) in primary care to address these complex needs, but their success largely depends on the competencies of healthcare professionals. Equipping primary care professionals with the competencies required for person-centred integrated care (PC-IC) is therefore essential.
